chunk_findings.detail: This hunk only erases the stray shard; nothing in the visible change adds the guard the bug explicitly requires ("Needs a guard in the test (refuse a repo not under tmp_path)"), and the deletion itself is indistinguishable from the loss that created the bug in the first place. The event stream shows the transcript test's `export.enabled`/`export.disabled` and gate events (lamport 70588–70635) were written into the primary's shard while the scripted session ran, i.e. the test resolved its repo to the primary because it inherited the primary's Lamport clock — which is exactly the "in-flight change of a fleet agent or an uncleared env" noted in the bug. Deleting the shard in this commit removes the evidence and the stray lamport entries, but if the test still resolves `--repo` from surroundings (e.g. a `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` or linked-worktree environment that this commit does not scrub), re-running `tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.py` after this change re-appends to `.ddflow/events/tx.jsonl` and re-creates the uncommitted `CL.md`, `[export.changelog] path='CL.md'` in `.ddflow/config.toml`, the stamped `.ddflow/.gitignore` region and `.ddflow/templates/` — so the commit undoes the symptom while the cause it names ("keep the test out of the primary tree") is unaddressed in the code shown. Because the deletion appears in the same change as (claimed) fixture edits that drop `review.fix_round_free` from the recorded `config`/`--explain` transcripts, and no replacement assertion on repo location is visible, this is a fix that cannot be demonstrated to fail-on-unfixed/pass-on-fixed for the stated defect; the guard must be present and pinned by a regression test, or the shard deletion is just log loss.
chunk_findings.title: .ddflow/events/tx.jsonl (deleted)

chunk_findings.detail: `scrub_git_env(monkeypatch)` and `assert_sandboxed(repo, tmp_path)` are inserted *after* the sandbox's own `git add` / `git commit` setup commands (lines 145-148), so the guard that is supposed to stop a redirected run cannot protect the first operations that a redirected run performs. Concretely: run pytest with a stray `GIT_DIR=/path/to/primary/.git` (no `GIT_WORK_TREE`) in the environment. git takes the cwd (`-C repo`) as the work tree, so `git -C repo add README.md` and `git commit -qm init` execute against the *primary's* `.git` — they write the/R EADME blob into the real index and create a commit on the real branch — and only then does `scrub_git_env` remove `GIT_DIR` and `assert_sandboxed` run. Because the scrub has already happened, the guard then sees `rev-parse --show-toplevel == repo`, passes, and reports nothing. This is exactly the failure class the change claims to close ("a test never appends events or writes files into the real project"), yet the guard/scrub ordering leaves the setup git commands unprotected; with `GIT_WORK_TREE` set they instead fail with `CalledProcessError` before the guard is ever consulted. The scrub (and the guard) must run before any git command touches the throwaway repo, i.e. before lines 145-148, not after them.

chunk_findings.detail: The change only reorders `scrub_git_env(monkeypatch)` so it runs before the three setup `git init` / `git add` / `git commit` calls. It does not touch the code path that actually produced the reported pollution. In the pre-change version, `scrub_git_env` already executed *before* `assert_sandboxed`, `monkeypatch.chdir(repo)`, the `DDFLOW_*` scrub loop, and — crucially — before the scripted session that appends to `.ddflow/events/*.jsonl` runs. So the env seen by the session (which is what resolves `--repo` and writes `tx.jsonl` / `pinhost-proj-7267fe.jsonl`, `.ddflow/config.toml`, `CL.md`) is identical before and after this diff; only the environment of the three setup git commands changed, and those commands never write `.ddflow/events/` or export config. Given the trigger, a `record` invocation with the environment that pollutes the primary still writes to the primary after this change, i.e. the fix is inert for the reported symptom. Consequently the required regression test would pass on the unfixed code, and `ddflow complete fix-sandbox-test-wrote-into-primary --regression-test <test>` would close the bug without a test that ever failed. The change also omits the guard the intent calls for (refuse a repo whose resolved root is not under `tmp_path`) and the cleanup of the stray shards already committed to `.ddflow/events/` — `assert_sandboxed(repo, tmp_path)` is passed `tmp_path / "proj"`, so a pure containment check on that value cannot fail and is not such a guard.

_printed_sha parses git commit's summary line; _is_ours removed; 18 door tests pass

chunk_findings.detail: The regex hardcodes the abbreviation length window 7..40, but the abbreviated sha git prints in the summary line is not fixed at 7: it follows `core.abbrev`, whose documented minimum is 4 (values 4–6 are legal). Given a repo/user config `core.abbrev = 4` (or 5/6), `git commit` prints e.g. `[main abcd] msg`; `re.findall` matches nothing, `_printed_sha` returns `None`, and the caller takes the `ours is None` branch and (a) emits the false note "event log not committed" and (b) skips the `_rebuild_on` remake for a commit that *was* successfully created — reintroducing exactly the residual-window symptom the change claims to fix. The same bound is wrong on the high side: in a SHA-256 repository with `core.abbrev` set above 40, the printed sha is longer than 40 hex chars and the pattern again fails, with the same consequence. The old `_is_ours` did not depend on the printed abbreviation length at all, so this is a new failure mode.

chunk_findings.detail: The new acceptance test is `found_tree == write-tree(index)`, and that tree is taken from the live index *after* `git commit` has already run its hooks, not from the commit object. `git commit` exports its index to the hooks it runs (`GIT_INDEX_FILE`, when set, is inherited), so any `post-commit`/`commit-msg` hook that stages something writes into exactly the index that `write-tree` later re-reads. In that case `built_tree` is the committed tree *plus* the hook's staged change, no printed summary sha has that tree, the loop in `_printed_sha` falls through and returns `None`, and `commit_shards` fails to recognise the commit it just made (the "not ours"/"could not check" outcome this change is meant to eliminate). The previous implementation — which only resolved the sha `git commit` printed and never touched the index — recognised it. Concrete input: a repo whose `.git/hooks/post-commit` is `#!/bin/sh\ngit add -u\n` (a common "format/stage on commit" hook); call `eventcommit.commit_shards(repo, "mine")` and `ours` is `None` even though the event commit landed. The same tree-plus-parent criterion also preserves the residual false positive named in the intent: a hook that prints the abbreviated sha of a same-tree, one-parent follow-up commit (e.g. an empty "trigger CI" commit) is preferred, because `_SUMMARY.findall(printed)` is walked in `reversed()` order.

chunk_findings.detail:
`_printed_sha` still decides "ours" by the very criterion the bug report says is not good enough — a one-parent commit holding the tree we just wrote — and it now does so with *less* information than before: the message part of the old identification is gone, and the candidate is chosen from every bracketed hex string in `git commit`'s captured output, last one first. The intent explicitly states that a foreign commit with the same tree must no longer be taken for ours ("a foreign commit with the same tree and a message starting the same way could be taken for ours ... Identify the commit by sha"), yet the new filter accepts exactly such a commit as long as it has one parent.

Concrete input, expressible with the new test's own harness: a `post-commit` hook (which runs, and prints, after git's `[branch sha] subject` summary) that mirrors the event commit and prints it, e.g. `echo "[$(git commit-tree $(git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}) -p HEAD)] mirrored"`. The mirror commit has (a) our tree and (b) exactly one parent, so in `_printed_sha` the reversed scan hits that hook line first and returns the mirror's sha — a commit `git commit` never created — instead of the sha in git's summary line. The caller then holds `ours` ≠ HEAD and re-makes the event commit (and in the residual window the same trick makes `_printed_sha` answer with a commit the door did not make). The docstring's own promise ("The full sha of the commit `git commit` says it made") is violated; only taking git's summary line, or building the object with `commit-tree`/CAS as the intent prescribes, would avoid it.

The test also never creates the race the fix describes: `foreign_commit_first` performs the foreign `other v2` commit *before* handing control to `real(...)`, so the door's commit lands on top as `HEAD`; the residual-window case — a foreign commit landing *after* the door's own commit, which is where the message-based `_is_ours` mis-answers — is never produced. Because the test asserts neither "the door's commit subject contains the hook prefix" nor "HEAD is the foreign commit rather than the door's", a passing run does not demonstrate that the regression path was exercised at all; it would keep passing if the hook silently stopped firing or if the intercated commit order changed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_events_committed_doors.py::test_a_commit_msg_hook_that_rewrites_the_subject_still_leaves_our_commit_known

chunk_findings.detail:
`_printed_sha` still decides "ours" by the very criterion the bug report says is not good enough — a one-parent commit holding the tree we just wrote — and it now does so with *less* information than before: the message part of the old identification is gone, and the candidate is chosen from every bracketed hex string in `git commit`'s captured output, last one first. The intent explicitly states that a foreign commit with the same tree must no longer be taken for ours ("a foreign commit with the same tree and a message starting the same way could be taken for ours ... Identify the commit by sha"), yet the new filter accepts exactly such a commit as long as it has one parent.

Concrete input, expressible with the new test's own harness: a `post-commit` hook (which runs, and prints, after git's `[branch sha] subject` summary) that mirrors the event commit and prints it, e.g. `echo "[$(git commit-tree $(git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}) -p HEAD)] mirrored"`. The mirror commit has (a) our tree and (b) exactly one parent, so in `_printed_sha` the reversed scan hits that hook line first and returns the mirror's sha — a commit `git commit` never created — instead of the sha in git's summary line. The caller then holds `ours` ≠ HEAD and re-makes the event commit (and in the residual window the same trick makes `_printed_sha` answer with a commit the door did not make). The docstring's own promise ("The full sha of the commit `git commit` says it made") is violated; only taking git's summary line, or building the object with `commit-tree`/CAS as the intent prescribes, would avoid it.
